chunks: Al-Saffar narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Abu Ja'far, from Abu Sa'd, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

If a man manumitted his female slave and then married her to a man and had intercourse with her, she would remain his slave and her children from him would be manumitted slaves, just as if a man went to a people and married their female slave, whatever was born to them would be slaves.

The correct interpretation of this report is that we understand it to mean that if it was stipulated upon him that the children be slaves, then they are indeed so; and they are only attached to freedom with manumission and the absence of a condition.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the children of a freed slave girl who marries a free man?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani's al-Ishtibār clarifies the juristic principle of *ilḥāq* (linking offspring status to the father) by addressing the specific case of a manumitted slave girl (*udhmā*) who marries a free man. While the default ruling is that her children are free, the text notes that they may remain slaves if a condition of slavery is explicitly stipulated, reflecting the interplay between manumission contracts and marital agreements in Shia fiqh. It further extends this logic to children born to a free woman who marries into a slave family, ensuring consistency in determining lineage status based on the father's condition and contractual stipulations.
